suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: updateEvent (and deleteEvent) fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` uses externalCalendarId which is falsy in that branch, so it never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined. WHY: When rescheduling/updating without an explicit externalCalendarId the code no longer falls back to the destination calendar and calendar.events.update/delete is called with undefined calendarId, failing to update/delete the event. HOW: Restore fallback to first destination or use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` or find by credentialId like createEvent does.

suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences undefined when destinationCalendar is null/empty. WHY: Destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined for empty array, then accessing `.integration` throws TypeError and crashes create() for events without a destination calendar. HOW: Use optional chaining `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` as the previous `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` safely did.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `Calendar.createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` now requires credentialId but LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService and BaseCalendarService still declare `createEvent(event)` with one param. WHY: Implementations no longer satisfy the interface, breaking type contract and CalendarManager now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` with an argument those services ignore/signature-mismatch, causing build errors and inconsistent calendar selection. HOW: Update all Calendar implementations to accept `credentialId: number` (even if unused) or make the param optional.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: createAllCalendarEvents/updateAllCalendarEvents fetch `prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id: destination.credentialId}})` when credential not in `calendarCredentials` without checking ownership. WHY: If destinationCalendar.credentialId is ever influenced by client-controlled data, any credential ID can be fetched and used to create/update calendar events under another user's/ team's identity (IDOR) bypassing the prior filter that limited to `this.calendarCredentials`. HOW: Verify fetched credential's userId/teamId matches the event owner/team before use, or restrict to credentials already in `calendarCredentials`.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `createAllCalendarEvents` iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` with `await createEvent` and `await prisma.credential.findUnique` per destination sequentially. WHY: For collective events with N hosts this issues N sequential DB queries and N sequential Google Calendar inserts instead of parallel, multiplying latency O(N) on the booking hot path. HOW: Collect promises and `await Promise.all` (and batch credential fetch with `findMany` where id in [...]) like the else-branch does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Null dereference on empty destinationCalendar. `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when no calendar is selected, then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws TypeError. Previously protected by `?.`. Fix with optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` and consider defaulting to true when undefined (or `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` with nullish check).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Broken fallback calendarId in updateEvent (and same pattern in deleteEvent 314-317). `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` when externalCalendarId is falsy compares against null/undefined and never matches, leaving selectedCalendar undefined. Should mirror createEvent logic: find by credentialId or fall back to mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.find(c=>c.externalId===externalCalendarId)?.externalId ?? mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number). This file still declares async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent) with one param — add credentialId param to satisfy contract and select correct calendar per credential (like Google via find(...credentialId)).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same contract break: Calendar.createEvent now requires (event, credentialId). Still declares async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent). Add credentialId param; otherwise CalendarManager.createEvent(event, credential.id) relies on ignored arg.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: After destinationCalendar became array, code does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar]=evt.destinationCalendar??[] then mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without ?. When array empty throws TypeError. Previous evt.destinationCalendar?.integration safely returned undefined. Fix to mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== 'google_calendar'.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: updateEvent fallback broken: selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal=>cal.externalId===externalCalendarId)?.externalId — in else branch externalCalendarId falsy so find never matches, always undefined. Previously fallback was event.destinationCalendar?.externalId. Same in deleteEvent 314-317. Fix to find by credentialId or mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Missing optional chaining after destructuring first destinationCalendar: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/undefined or [] (mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined). Original `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` safely treated missing as !=. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (and handle undefined case).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Dead else-branch in updateEvent: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal=>cal.externalId===externalCalendarId)?.externalId` - when externalCalendarId is falsy the find compares against that same falsy value and never matches, so selectedCalendar is always undefined instead of falling back to destinationCalendar[0].externalId. The createEvent fix correctly uses mainHostDestinationCalendar/outside find by credentialId. This will cause calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same dead else-branch in deleteEvent: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal=>cal.externalId===externalCalendarId)?.externalId` always yields undefined when externalCalendarId falsy. Should fallback to mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId like office365/lark do, otherwise calendar.events.delete is called with undefined calendarId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: updateEvent fallback is dead: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` - else branch runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so find comparison can never succeed. Should fallback to mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId or find by credentialId like createEvent does, not by the falsy externalCalendarId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: deleteEvent same dead else branch: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : find(cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` never matches because externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch. Fallback should be mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId (or credential-matched calendar), otherwise calendarId becomes undefined.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Missing optional chaining after destructure: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (... && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` throws when destinationCalendar is null/empty because mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. Original `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was safe. Change to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (or guard with `!mainHostDestinationCalendar` check).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Interface Calendar (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221) now requires createEvent(event, credentialId:number) and CalendarManager passes credential.id, but this class still declares createEvent(event: CalendarEvent) without credentialId. For collective events where evt.destinationCalendar has multiple entries, it always uses destinationCalendar[0] instead of finding the calendar matching credentialId (as GoogleCalendarService does via find(...credentialId)). Update signature to createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId:number) and select calendar by credentialId: destinationCalendar.find(c=>c.credentialId===credentialId)?.externalId || mainHost fallback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Producer handleNewBooking can set destinationCalendar to null (or [] when no calendar). Consumer here does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar]=evt.destinationCalendar??[]; then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without ?. When array is empty/null, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and .integration throws TypeError on every Meet-location booking without a destination calendar. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== 'google_calendar' (or guard with ?. ) to preserve original optional-chain semantics.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same contract mismatch as Office365: Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId:number) but this class still declares createEvent(event: CalendarEvent). Add credentialId param and select calendarId via destinationCalendar.find(c=>c.credentialId===credentialId)?.externalId instead of always using destinationCalendar[0], otherwise collective team events create all calendars on the first host's calendar.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: User-facing string bypasses i18n: calEvent.additionalNotes is set to hard-coded "Notes have been hidden by the organizer" (changed from organiser in this PR) with TODO comment. This note is shown in calendar events and is locale-specific English. Use the project's translation mechanism (e.g., translate/getTranslation) instead of a hard-coded literal, consistent with how other booking user-facing strings are localized.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires both isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner, not either. WHY: No user is both admin and owner simultaneously under normal roles, so this branch is effectively always false and legitimate team admins/owners are denied, falling back to organizer/attendee checks only. HOW: Change && to ||: (await isTeamAdmin(...)) || (await isTeamOwner(...)).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Duplicate/blacklist filtering is case-sensitive and does not dedupe within input array. WHY: guest === attendee.email and blacklisted.includes(guest) without lowercasing lets AddGuests with 'A@a.com' vs 'a@a.com' bypass dedupe/blacklist and create duplicate Attendee rows or bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS block; identical emails in the same request both pass through to createMany. HOW: Lowercase/normalize (trim+toLowerCase) guests and attendees before compare, and dedupe guests via Set before filtering, e.g., uniqueGuests = [...new Set(guests.map(g=>g.toLowerCase()))] filtered.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes original input array instead of filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: Guests that were duplicates/blacklisted and filtered out of DB still appear as newGuests in email-manager (newGuests.includes check line 541), causing wrong branching (AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail) and confusing new vs existing attendee semantics. HOW: Pass uniqueGuests (or guestsFullDetails emails) instead of raw guests.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: OrganizerAddGuestsEmail uses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name without guard. WHY: If booking has zero attendees (or all filtered), attendees[0] is undefined and accessing .name throws at email render time, crashing the post-update email step. HOW: Guard with attendees[0]?.name || organizer.name fallback and handle empty array.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: isInvalidEmail is set true on failed validation but never reset on input change or success path. WHY: Once user triggers an invalid submit, the error banner persists forever even after fixing emails, and validation with initial [''] plus length-0 early return gives no feedback when user deletes all fields. HOW: Reset isInvalidEmail to false onChange via useEffect on multiEmailValue or at start of handleAdd when validation succeeds.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts unbounded array of emails with no max length, trim, or normalize. WHY: Attacker (any authenticated attendee per handler line 52) can submit thousands of emails in one request, bypassing per-email checks via whitespace/case variants, amplifying DB writes (createMany), translation loading, and outbound email fanout in sendAddGuestsEmails. HOW: Add .max(10-25), .transform(s=>s.trim().toLowerCase()), and refine uniqueness at schema level.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: attendeesListPromises awaits getTranslation per attendee individually. WHY: For a booking with many attendees (or repeated adds), this triggers N parallel fs/i18n loads (O(N) I/O) on every addGuests call with no caching, compounding with unbounded Promise.all email sends. HOW: Batch or cache translations by locale (load each locale once) and reuse across attendees before Promise.all.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Case-sensitivity bypass in blacklist check: blacklistedGuestEmails are normalized to lower case (line 71 .toLowerCase()) but the incoming guest is compared without normalization via blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) at line 77. An attacker can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS by submitting Blocked@Example.com vs blocked@example.com. Fix: normalize guest to lower case before comparison (and for the duplicate check), e.g., guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase() and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase()).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Case-sensitive duplicate attendee check allows bypass: guest === attendee.email at line 76 compares case-insensitive emails case-sensitively. Submitting existing@example.com as Existing@Example.com passes the filter and creates a duplicate attendee record (also defeats the uniqueGuests dedup). Fix: compare lowercased forms: guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase().

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Client uniqueness validation is case-sensitive: ZAddGuestsInputSchema refine uses new Set(emails) size check without normalization. ['a@x.com','A@X.com'] is considered unique, allowing case-variant duplicates to be sent to the server (which also fails to dedup case-insensitively). Fix: normalize before Set, e.g., new Set(emails.map(e=>e.toLowerCase())).size === emails.length.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Logic error: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so a user must be BOTH admin and owner to pass. Should be ||. As written, team admins who are not owners (and vice versa) are incorrectly denied (FORBIDDEN at line 54) unless they are organizer/attendee.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Dead computation / wrong result: uniqueGuests is computed at lines 74-78 (filtering existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and used for DB insert, but sendAddGuestsEmails is called with original guests at line 168. Should pass uniqueGuests (lowercased consistently). Otherwise emails misclassify existing/blacklisted/duplicate addresses as new and newGuests.includes check in email-manager.ts is wrong.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Cross-reference inconsistency: client AddGuestsDialog.tsx validates guests with .refine(unique) while server ZAddGuestsInputSchema only checks z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check. Server handler’s filter also doesn’t dedupe duplicates within guests itself, so bypassing client validation can insert duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Check-then-create race + missing intra-request dedup allows duplicate Attendees and execution break: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees with case-sensitive `===` and against blacklisted list, but never deduplicates `guests` itself nor normalizes case, and the read (findFirst) and write (booking.update createMany) are non-atomic with no unique constraint handling. Two concurrent addGuests with same email or a single request with ["x@a.com","x@a.com"] or ["X@a.com","x@a.com"] both insert duplicate rows (state corruption) or throw Prisma P2002 unhandled. Fix: normalize to lower-case, dedupe with Set, and make insertion atomic — e.g., add unique index on (bookingId, email) if missing and handle conflict, or use transaction/upsert and validate `uniqueGuests` after normalization.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Server input schema permits duplicate/invalid invariants that client rejects: `z.array(z.string().email())` allows duplicate emails and empty array, unlike client schema which refines `uniqueEmails.size === emails.length`. A crafted request bypasses client and reaches handler with duplicates, causing duplicate createMany (state corruption) or DB unique-constraint exception (unhandled execution break at JSON-encode/Prisma layer). Fix: add `.refine` for uniqueness (and optionally `.nonempty().max(N)`) mirroring client, and normalize emails to lower-case before validation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Tooltip content is hard-coded English content="Remove email" while the same file uses useLocale/t("add_another") for other user-visible strings. This bypasses the translation mechanism established in the surrounding code. Replace with t("remove_email") (and add the key to locales) to match neighbouring strings.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Menu entry id is "add_members" but the feature is AddGuests/addGuests throughout the PR (AddGuestsDialog, trpc addGuests mutation). The name states members while the code adds booking guests/attendees, making the identifier untrue and inconsistent with its label t("additional_guests"). Rename id (and corresponding data-testid in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:98) to "add_guests".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Handler passes original `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails while only `uniqueGuests` were actually created. The consumer (email-manager.ts:sendAddGuestsEmails) partitions attendees by `newGuests.includes` to choose AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass the filtered array (`uniqueGuests`) instead of `guests` so only truly added guests are treated as new.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: encodeOAuthState is identical to decodeOAuthState (JSON.parse then JSON.stringify of req.query.state) and never builds state from req.query.teamId/returnTo. WHY: Add handlers call encodeOAuthState(req) expecting it to encode team context into the OAuth state param; with this impl state is undefined unless the incoming request already has ?state=, so team OAuth and returnTo are lost and callbacks create personal credentials instead of team ones. HOW: Restore original logic that constructs { teamId, returnTo, installGoogleVideo } from query and returns JSON.stringify(state).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: decodeOAuthState calls JSON.parse(req.query.state) without try/catch. WHY: Attacker-controlled ?state=notjson throws SyntaxError uncaught, crashing every OAuth callback that uses this helper (google, hubspot, salesforce etc) with 500 instead of 400. HOW: Wrap JSON.parse in try/catch and return undefined or throw HttpError 400.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] which evaluate to "[object Object]", so schema only validates access_token and ignores expiry fields. WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the parser accepts any response with access_token, then downstream code fakes missing refresh_token with placeholder "refresh_token" and stores corrupted expiry_date. HOW: Replace with z.record or .passthrough or proper zod shape e.g. z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: googleCalendarService does const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) and stores { success, data } wrapper as credential key instead of key.data. WHY: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse result; storing wrapper corrupts credential so next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails and refresh loop breaks. HOW: Store parseResult.data (or use .data) and handle !success branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns fetch Response, but callers expect provider-specific shapes (google expects {res:{data}}, Zoho expects axios {data:{}}}). WHY: googleCalendar does token=res?.data (undefined with fetch), Zoho Bigin/Crm do tokenInfo.data.error (TypeError on fetch Response), so token refresh wipes access_token or crashes. HOW: Normalize return: fetch then handleErrorsJson/json and return data shape callers expect, or branch per caller.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Bigin refresh passes credentialId (credential.id) as third arg to refreshOAuthTokens which expects userId, so fetch sends calcomUserId=credentialId. WHY: External sync endpoint looks up wrong user, refresh fails or returns wrong tokens, and credential update uses wrong identity. HOW: Pass credential.userId or credentialKey user association instead of credentialId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: File uses prisma.credential.update but never imports prisma, and bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely for Salesforce. WHY: Runtime ReferenceError on every Salesforce getClient call; also inconsistent with credential sync feature and statusText check (response.statusText !== "OK") is unreliable. HOW: Add import prisma from "@calcom/prisma" and route through refreshOAuthTokens or handle fetch errors correctly.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Webhook secret check uses !== without timing-safe compare, header name lookup is case-sensitive, and handler has no method check, allowing GET to overwrite any userId credential (IDOR) if secret is known. WHY: Header lookup req.headers[envName || "calcom-webhook-secret"] fails if admin sets mixed-case name; timing-unsafe compare leaks secret via side channel; missing if(req.method!=="POST") lets crawlers/CSRF trigger writes. HOW: Normalize header name toLowerCase, use crypto.timingSafeEqual, enforce POST, and verify caller authorization for userId.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Decrypt uses symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "") then JSON.parse without try/catch or key-length validation. WHY: Invalid base64/aes key throws and crashes with 500, leaking stack; empty fallback key would decrypt with wrong key and produce garbage that is stored as credential. HOW: Validate env key length (32 bytes), catch decrypt/parse errors and return 400.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Sync path does await fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) with no timeout/abort or error handling on the hot token-refresh path. WHY: Every calendar availability/meeting create blocks on external endpoint; slow or hanging endpoint stalls all CalendarService calls and can exhaust event-loop requests. HOW: Add AbortController timeout (e.g. 5s), handle non-200 responses, and fallback to direct refresh on failure.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Timing attack: webhook secret compared with !==. Use constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers after hashing/length check) instead of direct string !== to avoid leaking secret via execution time.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Insecure fallback for encryption key: symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "") supplies empty string if env missing. For 32-byte AES256 key this is a weak default; fail-fast (throw/403) when key is absent instead of decrypting with "".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse now returns a Zod SafeParse result {success,data}, not parsed data. Code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and stores `key` directly as credential.key. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` returned plain credentials. Will persist {success:true,data:{...}} wrapper instead of tokens, breaking subsequent auth.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Changed behavioural contract: when sharing enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Consumers not updated: Hubspot expects HubspotToken object, Bigin/Zohocrm expect AxiosResponse with .data, Lark/Office365/Webex/Zoom expect fetch Response body handling. Hubspot does `const hubspotRefreshToken:HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and later accesses token fields directly - with sharing enabled it holds a Response and will fail / store wrong shape.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Third param contract is userId:number|null (used as calcomUserId for sync endpoint). Call site passes `credentialId` (credential primary key) instead of `credential.userId` like every other CalendarService. When sharing enabled, sync request is sent with wrong id and non-user credential refresh will incorrectly try sync path. Also expects Axios response with .data.error but sharing path returns fetch Response with no .data.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: New encodeOAuthState is identical to decodeOAuthState - it requires `req.query.state` string and returns JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(state)). Original add.ts flows called encodeOAuthState to embed teamId/other state into the OAuth redirect URL when no query state exists. Now returns undefined for normal add requests, dropping team context and breaking team OAuth installs. Reconstructing before: encode built state from request/body; after: it just echoes incoming query.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: JSDoc duplicates param description: both @param appData.type and @param appData.appId are described as "the app slug". In code appData.type is stored as credential.type while appId is the slug. Update docs to reflect distinct meaning, e.g. @param appData.type credential type and @param appData.appId app slug.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Comment says key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24` which generates 24 bytes. Either require 24 bytes or suggest `openssl rand -base64 32` (32 bytes). Align documented requirement with generation command.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Comment says schema should accept any numeric expiry property and allow other properties, but code uses [z.string().toString()] computed keys which creates literal keys like "ZodString", not a Zod catchall. Replace with .catchall(z.number())/.passthrough() or z.record() to match documented intent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Function named encodeOAuthState reads req.query.state, JSON.parses then JSON.stringifies — essentially decode+identity, identical to decodeOAuthState except stringify. Callers in .../api/add.ts use it to encode outbound OAuth state; it should encode a state object to a string, not re-encode inbound query state. Rename or rewrite to encode supplied state, e.g. encodeOAuthState(state: IntegrationOAuthCallbackState): string.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Cross-reference inconsistency: refreshOAuthTokens expects userId as 3rd arg (used as calcomUserId for the sync endpoint), but zoho-bigin passes credentialId (credential.id) instead of credential.userId. Every other CalendarService (google, hubspot, lark, office365calendar, office365video, webex, zohocrm, zoom) passes credential.userId. This sends the credential PK to the external sync endpoint as if it were a user, breaking sync and querying the wrong principal. Pass credential.userId (capture it from CredentialPayload) instead of credentialId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Incorrect measurement / wrong schema: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] which evaluate to static strings (e.g. "ZodString"), not a wildcard for any expiry field. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so expires_in / expiry_date / expiresIn etc. are dropped when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, so callers then read undefined expiry. Use z.record, .passthrough() or .catchall(z.number()) instead of computed property.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Dead computation / copy-paste error: encodeOAuthState is identical to decodeOAuthState except for a final JSON.stringify. It parses req.query.state and re-stringifies the same value (identity transform) without enrichment. This computes a value and returns the original untransformed value, indicating the intended encoding (e.g., adding teamId / base64) was lost in the move to oauth/ folder. Compare with intended encode behavior and restore transformation vs just echoing input.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Producer `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch Response` when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, but this consumer does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(()=> fetchTokens.res, ...); const token = res?.data` assuming the googleapis `{data:...}` shape. When sync is enabled `res.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Fix: normalize `refreshOAuthTokens` to return parsed JSON in a consistent shape, or handle both branches here (e.g., `const raw = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = (raw as any)?.data ?? await (raw as Response).json()`), consistent with how office365calendar/zoom handle the Response via `handleErrorsJson`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This producer returns heterogeneous types: `fetch Response` when syncing, vs whatever `refreshFunction` returns (HubspotToken object, axios `{data}` object, google `{res:{data}}`). Consumers added in this PR that wrap axios (`zoho-bigin` `axios.post`, `zohocrm` `axios({...})`) or hubspot SDK (`hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken`) do `tokenInfo.data` / treat result as `HubspotToken` without JSON-parsing a Response, so when sync is enabled they get a fetch Response and crash on `undefined.data`. Fix the contract: either always return parsed JSON (e.g., `return response.json()`) or document and enforce that callers must handle Response, and update zoho-bigin, zohocrm, hubspot to parse the Response (`await response.json()` / `handleErrorsJson`) like office365/zoom do.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: TOCTOU race: findFirst then create/update without transaction or unique constraint. Two concurrent webhooks for same userId+appId both find no row and both attempt create, resulting in duplicate credentials or Prisma P2002 unique violation (500). Use atomic upsert (upsert with compound unique @@unique([userId,appId]) or transaction with serializable lock) instead of findThenCreate.

suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Password is not verified when both totpCode and backupCode are supplied. The check `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` gates verifyPassword on absence of totpCode, but the backupCode branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` is taken first and never verifies password. WHY: An attacker with a stolen backup code can bypass password by sending email + valid backupCode + dummy totpCode (e.g. totpCode='123456') + empty/wrong password; `!credentials.totpCode` is false so verifyPassword is skipped and backupCode alone grants login. HOW: Always verify password when credentials.password is expected, or change gate to `!credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode` and explicitly verify password inside the backupCode branch before accepting the code.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Backup-code single-use is enforced with non-atomic read-modify-write: `indexOf` then `backupCodes[index]=null` then `prisma.user.update` without a conditional write. WHY: Two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass `indexOf !== -1` before either update, allowing reuse of a supposedly single-use code and violating the security invariant. HOW: Use an atomic update (transaction with `SELECT FOR UPDATE` or `WHERE backupCodes = oldValue` optimistic check) or remove the used code and fail if the update affects 0 rows.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Backup-codes download URL created with `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked when a new URL overwrites it; `resetState` and unmount never call `URL.revokeObjectURL`. WHY: Each 2FA setup leaves an unreleased Blob URL in memory; repeated open/close cycles leak object URLs and Blob memory until page reload. HOW: Revoke in `resetState` and in a `useEffect` cleanup that revokes `backupCodesUrl` on change/unmount.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Toggle button for 'Lost access' inside `<Form>` has no `type="button"` and sits alongside the submit button. WHY: Default button type inside a form is submit, so clicking 'Lost access' can trigger `handleDisable` with empty/partial codes, showing spurious errors and submitting unintended data. HOW: Add `type="button"` to the toggle button (and ensure it calls `preventDefault` or is outside form submit).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup-code verification uses Array.indexOf with === (line 61: backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))). This is not constant-time and leaks timing info about secret prefix. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual over buffers after hashing/normalizing length) looping over all candidates without early exit.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup-code verification uses Array.indexOf with === (line 144: backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))). This is not constant-time and leaks timing info. Replace with constant-time comparison (timingSafeEqual) over all stored codes, e.g., compare hashed/normalized buffers and accumulate result without early return.

suggestions.suggestionContent: Race condition TOCTOU on backup-code reuse: handler reads decrypts array, checks indexOf, then sets index to null and UPDATEs. Two concurrent authorize calls with same code both read array containing code, both pass index!=-1, both set null and succeed, allowing 'single-use' code to be used twice. WHY: Any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g., 'https://', 'disc') passes, allowing a malicious page to send fake discourse-resize messages and control iframe height or future message handlers. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method==raw_html, bypassing PostAnalyzer sanitization, and best.html.erb renders it with <%= raw post.cooked %>. WHY: Content imported from RSS/remote readability is stored as raw_html and rendered unsanitized inside the embed iframe, giving stored XSS from any compromised or malicious feed. WHY: An attacker who controls feed_polling_url or embed_url (via embed controller) can probe internal network/metadata IPs and hang workers with slow responses. HOW: Use FinalDestination/Net::HTTP with SSRF blocklist, redirected host validation, and open timeouts.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: perform_retrieve synchronously instantiates Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) on every embed cache miss. WHY: Each new embed_url triggers a full synchronous RSS fetch + parsing + N sequential TopicEmbed.import DB writes inside the RetrieveTopic job, blocking the job queue and amplifying load (hourly job becomes per-request). HOW: Remove inline poll or make it async/limited to one item lookup.

WHY: postMessage will fail with Invalid target origin when referer contains path, and leaks full referer; spec expects origin like https://host[:port]. HOW: Use request.referer origin (URI(request.referer).scheme+host+port) or '*' / Discourse.base_url origin, and guard nil.

suggestions.suggestionContent: Race / invariant violation: import checks TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first then creates TopicEmbed inside transaction. One raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled execution break) and duplicate topics can be created. Fix with upsert/find_or_create with lock or rescue RecordNotUnique and retry lookup.

suggestions.suggestionContent: Unhandled exception from network/parse: SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) can raise OpenURI::HTTPError, SocketError, Timeout::Error or parse errors. No rescue so poll_feed job throws and stops. Wrap open/parse in rescue and log/return.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Origin validation is reversed and uses substring search: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 . Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. "http", "https", "/") passes. suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (md5 of view class names, deterministic static value) instead of per-request random token. WHY: Attacker can predict state (same for all users/sessions) and forge/replay OAuth callback, bypassing CSRF protection that OAuth2LoginView provides via secrets.token_hex(). HOW: Generate random state per pipeline (secrets.token_hex), store via pipeline.bind_state("state", state) and validate against that, like OAuth2CallbackView does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: safe_urlopen and get_user_info calls have no exception handling; get_user_info calls raise_for_status(). WHY: Network failure, 401, or timeout raises unhandled exception bubbling to 500 instead of rendering integration-failed page; contrasts with OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token which catches SSLError/ConnectionError/JSON errors. HOW: Wrap safe_urlopen/safe_urlread/get_user_info in try/except and return error(request, active_organization) on any exception.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Direct access integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] without .get() guards. WHY: Existing integrations created before this change or via other paths may lack metadata["sender"], causing KeyError 500 instead of graceful invalid-request error. HOW: Use integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login") and treat missing as verification failure -> return error().

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: First-time installation (Integration.DoesNotExist) returns pipeline.next_step() without verifying authenticated GitHub user matches installer. WHY: Attacker can obtain a fresh GitHub App installation_id and claim it on a victim Sentry org; the mismatch check at 500-505 only runs when Integration already exists (second-org claim), so initial claim is unverified. HOW: Also verify on creation path, e.g., fetch installation info or require sender metadata and compare to github_authenticated_user, or block DoesNotExist if github_authenticated_user is missing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: safe_urlopen and get_user_info are outside the try/except that only wraps safe_urlread. If GitHub token exchange fails (network error, non-2xx, invalid code) safe_urlopen raises, and get_user_info can raise on API errors, both propagate as unhandled 500. Wrap the exchange (safe_urlopen + safe_urlread + get_user_info) in a single try/except and return error(request, self.active_organization) on any exception, matching the handling for missing access_token/login.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] uses direct indexing. If integration was created by old webhook payload, migration, or malformed metadata missing sender/login, this raises KeyError/TypeError and crashes the installation pipeline (500). Use .get() chain with guard: sender = (integration.metadata or {}).get("sender", {}); login = sender.get("login"); if login is None or login != pipeline.fetch_state(...): return error(...).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: User-facing strings bypass translation extraction: error() uses _(error_short) with a variable (line 141) and default/call-site literals are plain strings ("Invalid installation request.", "GitHub installation pending deletion.", "Github installed on another Sentry organization."). Extraction tools only pick up _("<literal>"). Make each literal extractable by using _("<literal>") at definition/call site and remove the _(variable) indirection (e.g., define constants ERR_* = _("..." ) for the short messages or pass already-translated values).
